newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Mar 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Mar 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a surprise move last night, the David Jones announced the upmarket retailer's chief executive, Chris Tideman, who joined the company in 1994, is resigning amid concerns in the market about the direction of David Jones Ltd. Tideman will be returning to the United Kingdom. Page 1.

In a submission to the Government's business program review, the Industry Commission has called for an environment which facilitates high and sustainable growth. The IC stepped up its campaign to streamline the Commonwealth's $3 billion-plus business assstance program. Page 5.

Following the resignation of former managing director John Dougall last September, gaming and wagering group AWA Ltd has - under a comprehensive overhaul headed by Tim Hughes, the head of Reg Grundy's RG Capital Pty Ltd - announced a major board reshuffleand dumped plans to expand its poker machine business. Page 21.

In a move which will see the wholesale price of four labels cut substantially in the next few weeks, Lion Nathan has finalised a new strategy for several brands. The plan, which could trigger another round of discounting between Lion and Foster's Brewing roup, will see Lion's Tooheys Red and Tooheys Blue labels included in its "price brand" portfolio. Page 21.

In a move which could signal peace between telecommunications giants Seven Network Ltd and cable television group Optus Vision, Optus Vision group shareholders - including Seven, Optus Communications, US West And Publishing & Broadcasting - have agreed toextend the deadline under which Optus, US West and PBL were due to transfer their shares in Optus Vision to Seven. Page 23.

Speaking at Orogen Minerals' release of results for the eight months to December 31, Orogen managing director Charles Lepani said the Papua New Guinea Government's plans to buy back Bougainville Copper from RTZ-CRA had progressed further than expected and could lead to a decision within the next 18 months on Orogen taking up its option on the project. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a brief statement after the stockmarket closed, David Jones chairman Dick Warburton revealed Chris Tideman, who joined the upmarket retailer in 1994 and presided over the float in 1995, had resigned as chief executive for "personal reasons". The move cmes amid mounting pressure on David Jones' profits and overall strategic position. Page 19.

Former Consolidated Press Ltd managing director Trevor Kennedy is among three new directors appointed to replace five departing members of the AWA Ltd board. Kennedy has been appointed chairman at AWA as part of a major boardroom shake-up, which the gaming and communications group hopes will complete its transformation. Page 19.

For the first time a bank or financial institution has been able to offer a fixed rate loan for such a term, banking and finance group Colonial has launched a 15-year fixed rate loan, priced at just under 10 per cent a year. The launch signifies the firstmoves to shake-up Australia's long-term lending market. Page 19.

Ross Mining NL yesterday rejected compensation claims by land owners in the Solomon Islands who threaten to delay work on the company's gold mining project. Managing director Bertus de Graaf said the company was proud of its record in the Solomon Islands An application for compensation was lodged in the Solomon Islands High Court yesterday. Page 19.

Despite a net loss of $A16 million on a computer software write-off, newly formed Suncorp-Metway Ltd has posted a December-half profit of A$34 million. However, the company has refused to say whether the $A170.8 million 1997 profit, forecast in the indepndent expert's merger report, was achievable. Page 21.

Austrade is hoping the inclusion of more than 70 Australian wine makers in Tokyo's annual food expo will inspire a renewed marketing drive in Japan. Tokyo marketing officer Charles Davidson said that due to the growing popularity of wine in Japan, it wasno longer a market Australian wine producers could ignore. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Stockbroking analysts were last night predicting an Australian-based retailer from either Coles Myer or Woolworths would be the likely successor as chief executive of David Jones following the surprise resignation of Chris Tideman from the position. Tideman's resignation comes just two days before the company is expected to reveal a 50 per cent drop in profit for the January half-year. Page 25.

In a move described by Mackay Refined Sugar chief executive Jim Hughes as "intriguing", Federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson has established the Sugar Taskforce to look into the sugar industry's future, with one of its specific tasks to "explore" the potential merger of ailing refined sugar operations MRS and CSR. Page 25.

After Orogen Minerals yesterday posted a maiden net profit of 16.42 million kina (A$15.2 million) surpassing the forecast of 12.6 million kina for the eight months from May 1 in the prospectus for the company's A$260 million float, Orogen managing director Charles Lepani said the company would not become a dumping ground for the Papua New Guinea Government's difficult resources investments. Page 25.

AWA's major shareholder, Reg Grundy's RG Capital, has played a significant role in the shedding of five directors from the board - John Iliffe resigned yesterday as AWA chairman and directors David Greatorex, David Parkin, Grahame Campbell and Robert Frater have also left the board, as the company recorded a A$15.7 million loss for the half-year to December. Page 25.

Advertising agency Saatchi and Saatchi has landed the A$7 million dollar Sanitarium Health Food account. The move has left the company's previous advertiser, The Campaign Palace, with a massive hole in their books. Saatchi has handled Sanitarium's Weet-ix campaign for the past two years. Page 27.

Tasmania's Trust Bank is to be sold off in a combined trade sale and public float. The Tasmanian Government has agreed to allow the bank to search for a "strategic partner" to buy 49 per cent before selling another 41 per cent to the public. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a move coming two days before the confirmation of a sharp downturn in David Jones' earnings for the half-year to January 25, chief executive Chris Tideman resigned last night, ending months of pressure over the upmarket retailer's poor performance. A satement about a replacement for the position is expected soon. Page B1.

In a corporatisation based on the West Australian Government's sale of BankWest to Bank of Scotland in 1995, Tasmania's Trust Bank, the State's biggest bank with almost 42 per cent of Tasmania's deposit business, is seeking a strategic shareholder to acqure 49 per cent of the bank, with the remaining shares to be sold off in a public offer in the middle of 1998. Page B1.

Figures released yesterday by the Department of Transport show Qantas Airways has successfully maintained its share of passengers flying in and out of Australia, despite tough competition from the Japanese market. It has also posted a sharp rise in passeger numbers on international routes. Page B3.

Allegations of illegal wire tapping are amongst an extended tax-fraud probe into the Israeli subsidiary of Rupert Murdoch's media empire. Officials yesterday confirmed reports but denied that the subsidiary's chief executive, Abraham Peled, had been arreted a week ago. Page B3.

A bid to stop an Australian gold mining project has been launched by indigenous land owners in the Solomon Island courts. The Brisbane-based Ross Mining NL was notified of the legal attempts just two days before they were to receive their mining lease frm the Solomons Government. Page B3.

Posting a maiden net profit of $A15.2 million Orogen Minerals managing director Charles Lepani said yesterday the company would not become a dumping ground for the Papua New Guinean Government's difficult resources investments. The PNG Government retainsa 51.7 per cent controlling stake after privatisation took place last year. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
